concepts.why: The patient presented with respiratory rate of 27 breaths/min, oxygen saturation of 95% on a nonrebreather mask, and pulmonary consolidation, indicating respiratory failure.
The patient's pulse rate was in the 20s and heart rate was 49 beats/min, indicating bradycardia.
The patient's blood pressure was 100/73 mm Hg, indicating hypotension.
The patient presented with pulmonary consolidation, indicating pneumonia.
The patient presented with respiratory failure, hypotension, and pneumonia, indicating severe sepsis.
The patient presented with respiratory failure, pulmonary consolidation, and hypoxemia, indicating ARDS.
The computed tomography of the head showed no acute pathology, which rules out intracranial hemorrhage as a cause of the patient's symptoms.

rationales.F12: Pulmonary consolidation is a strong indicator of pneumonia and can also be seen in severe sepsis and ARDS.
